---
title: "The R package"
---

```{r}
#| label: load
m <- read.csv("../releases/manifest.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = "character")
cur <- m[nrow(m), ]
core_cols <- setdiff(grep("_redivis_version$", names(m), value = TRUE), "eco_meta_redivis_version")
core_tags <- function(r) {
  v <- unlist(r[core_cols]); v <- v[!is.na(v) & nzchar(v)]
  paste(sub("_redivis_version$", "", names(v)), v, collapse = ", ")
}
```

The `eco` R package reads the warehouse from R with **no account or token**.
Every table on Redivis is served as CSV to anyone, within Redivis' 100 MB
cap on anonymous requests. Most eco tables are far under it; the few that are
not need a free Redivis login (see [Large tables](#large-tables)).

```r
remotes::install_github("ben-domingue/eco", subdir = "Rpkg")
library(eco)
```

## Thirty seconds

```r
eco_list_tables()                                   # what is there
eco_filter(model_family = "occupancy", min_units = 30)
eco_info("schank_2015_tapir_occ")                   # dims, family, licence, citation

umf <- eco_filter(model_family = "Single-season occupancy") |>
  head(1) |> eco_fetch() |> eco_to_unmarked()
unmarked::occu(~1 ~1, umf)
```

`eco_fetch()` of one table returns a data.frame in the format described on the
[standard](standard.html) page; of several (a filter result or a character
vector) a named list. The side tables come from `eco_taxa()`, `eco_periods()`,
`eco_units()` and `eco_traps()`.

## Functions

| | |
|---|---|
| `eco_list_tables()`, `eco_list_deposits()`, `eco_metadata()`, `eco_biblio()`, `eco_tags()`, `eco_tag_options()` | the corpus and its descriptions, from the `eco_meta` dataset; `eco_list_deposits()` is one row per source deposit with the tables built from it |
| `eco_filter(model_family=, response_type=, taxon_group=, protocol=, min_units=, min_occasions=, multi_species=, sample_floor=, licence=)` | choose tables; `licence = "permissive"` keeps tables open to commercial use ([Using eco responsibly](https://ben-domingue.github.io/eco/use.html)) |
| `eco_fetch(x)`; `eco_taxa()`, `eco_periods()`, `eco_units()`, `eco_traps()` | a table and its side tables |
| `eco_info(table)` | one table, or the corpus totals |
| `eco_to_array()`, `eco_to_unmarked()`, `eco_to_ch()` and the inverses `array_to_eco()`, `umf_to_eco()`, `mpois_to_eco()`, `ch_to_eco()` | reshape to and from `unmarked` frames, arrays and capture histories |
| `eco_check(df)` | the R twin of the validator, for a table you built |
| `eco_to_irw(df)` | the IRW v1.0 view (`id`, `item`, `resp`, `cov_*`) |
| `eco_cite(tables, format = "text"/"bibtex", file=)` | cite the original deposits and papers, and eco (see [How to cite](#how-to-cite)); `eco_save_bibtex(tables, file)` is the BibTeX shortcut |
| `eco_version()`, `eco_set_version(n)`, `eco_reset_version()`, `eco_manifest()` | pin a release |
| `eco_cache_dir()`, `eco_cache_info()`, `eco_clear_cache()` | the disk cache under `tools::R_user_dir("eco", "cache")` |

## Versions

Redivis versions each dataset separately (the core tables are split across
the shards `eco`, `eco_2`, ..., because Redivis caps a dataset at 1000 entries, side tables included; then
`eco_meta`); the [release manifest](corrections.html) pairs them into numbered
eco versions. By default the package reads the current release of each (now eco
v`r cur$eco_version`: Redivis `r core_tags(cur)`, `eco_meta`
`r cur$eco_meta_redivis_version`). `eco_set_version(1)` pins all of them to what eco
version 1 consisted of, so a script reproduces what it read then. Tables the
pipeline has built but Redivis has not yet released are not offered by
`eco_filter()`; they are listed in `attr(eco_metadata(), "unreleased")`.

## How to cite {#how-to-cite}

Every eco table rests on fieldwork by the people who deposited it. **Cite the
original deposit, and its paper, for every table you use**, and eco as well. A
paper that cites only eco gives the credit for the data to the warehouse.

```r
tabs <- eco_filter(taxon_group = "Amphibians", min_units = 30)
eco_cite(tabs)                                   # a reference list
eco_cite(tabs, "bibtex", file = "eco_sources.bib")
```

`eco_cite()` gives one entry per source deposit and one per paper, not one per
table: tables built from the same deposit share an entry. BibTeX keys are
stable (the deposit's first table name, and `<that>_paper` for the paper), so
re-running it does not break a manuscript. The last entry is eco at the
version you read (`eco_version()`, which you should also state). For a paper
that uses many tables, put the file in a supplement and cite it from the
methods. The first `eco_fetch()` in a session prints a one-line reminder;
`options(eco.cite_reminder = FALSE)` silences it.

From Python, without the package, the same columns are in the `biblio` table
of `eco_meta`:

```python
import pandas as pd
ua = {"User-Agent": "eco-python (https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco)"}
b = pd.read_csv("https://redivis.com/api/v1/tables/datapages.eco_meta.biblio/rows?format=csv",
                storage_options=ua)
used = b[b.table.isin(["kery_2008_willowtit_occ", "schank_2015_tapir_occ"])]
refs = sorted(set(used.citation) | set(used.reference.dropna()))   # deposits and papers
```

This is per table, so it can list a deposit twice (with and without its DOI,
say) and `bibtex` is keyed by table; `eco_cite()` in R is the one that
removes duplicates.

## Large tables

A few tables are bigger than the 100 MB Redivis serves without a login:
`eco_list_tables()` marks them `needs_login`, and `eco_info()` says so. For
those `eco_fetch()` uses the `redivis`
client. That needs a free Redivis
account and two more packages, once:

```r
install.packages(c("redivis", "arrow"))
redivis::redivis$authenticate()        # opens a browser; or set REDIVIS_API_TOKEN
eco_fetch("rooney_2025_snapshotusa_comm")
```

The download counts against the account's Redivis export quota and is cached
like any other table, so it happens once per version. Without a login
`eco_fetch()` stops and says what to do; it never opens a browser by itself.

## Offline

`schank_2015_tapir_occ` (22 cameras, 72 days, one Endangered tapir with
coarsened coordinates, 1,008 rows) ships with the package so the converters
can be tried without a network:

```r
eco_to_unmarked(schank_2015_tapir_occ) |> unmarked::occu(~1 ~1, data = _)
```

Source: [`Rpkg/`](https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco/tree/main/Rpkg).
